images.filename: Path and Line run in Tandem - geograph.org.uk - 244267.jpg
images.caption: Path and Line run in Tandem. This photograph shows the Llanberis Path and the Snowdon Mountain Railway track as they climb up the slope in the direction of Half Way House and Half Way Station respectively. In the foreground the railway line runs below the path. In the middle ground the railway crosses the path by means of a bridge and climbs above it to Half Way Station (both hidden in this view). The path continues on towards Half Way House which can be seen clearly.
images.alt: Path and Line run in Tandem. images.filename: Caterpillar digger on Snowdon Mountain Railway - geograph.org.uk - 1174826.jpg
images.caption: Caterpillar digger on Snowdon Mountain Railway This digger is the means by which the rail track is dug out of the winter snow.  There is still a significant amount of snow to be moved before it reaches the station.  The shadowy figures of walkers can be seen on the path above the railway.

images.filename: Danger-Perygl on the Snowdon Mountain Railway - geograph.org.uk - 1174932.jpg
images.caption: Danger/Perygl on the Snowdon Mountain Railway It is not immediately obvious but the track of the Snowdon Mountain Railway is beneath the snow here.  The 'Danger/Perygl' sign is to warn walkers to stay clear of the track when the trains are running.  They were not running on this day.  The path to the summit can be seen on the right.

images.filename: New station building on Yr Wyddfa - geograph.org.uk - 1174963.jpg
images.caption: New station building on Yr Wyddfa The new station building and platform, which has been built to serve the Snowdon Mountain Railway, looks particularly grey on this misty day. images.filename: Awyrlun o Gastell y Bere yn Hydref 2024 - Aerial image of Welsh castle Castell y Bere near Tywyn, Gwynedd, Wales 50.png
images.caption:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
Castell y Bere is a Welsh castle in south Gwynedd, Wales. It was one of the most important castles of the princes of Gwynedd in the 13th century. It was built by Llywelyn the Great to keep out the invading English. It is believed that the poet Gruffudd ab yr Ynad Goch composed his famous elegy for Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (Llywelyn II) in Castell y Bere in December 1282 or early 1283.
images.alt:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
